A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete TIMotion paper, including Appendices A–E and references. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original TIMotion evaluations on InterHuman and InterX, component ablations, computational measurements, and motion in-betweening results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original TIMotion experiments, including InterHuman results in Table 1, InterX results in Table 7, and the ablation and editing evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Causal Interactive Injection, Role-Evolving Scanning, Localized Pattern Amplification, and loss formulations. The motion in-betweening inference procedure in Appendix B is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-conditioned human-human motion generation on InterHuman and InterX and motion in-betweening on InterHuman. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding table, including the ComMDM variants in Table 1, temporal-modeling alternatives in Table 2, InterGen in Table 6, and T2M*, MDM(GRU), and InterGen* in Table 7.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation settings in Section 4 and Appendices A–D are identical. These include the evaluation metrics, 1500-epoch training budget, 50-step DDIM sampling, and in-betweening evaluation that generates the middle 80% from the first and last 10%.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, normalization and convolution-kernel comparisons, motion-frequency analysis, computational comparison, and qualitative examples. Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–7 contain no added or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Both report 20 evaluations and means with 95% confidence intervals in Section 4.2.1 and Appendix A. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are identical. For example, TIMotion+RWKV retains InterHuman FID 4.702 ± 0.069 and Top-1 R-Precision 0.501 ± 0.005 in Table 1, and InterX FID 0.261 ± 0.0140 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13, including the diffusion formulation, causal-sequence definitions, objectives, and appendix metric formulas, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about MetaMotion, TIMotion's three components, compatibility with Transformer/Mamba/RWKV, computational efficiency, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal modeling, evolving interaction roles, and LPA-induced smoothness are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning dataset/task variety and unexplored interactions among three or more people.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including CLIP-ViT-L/14, embedding dimensions, optimizer settings, loss weights, batch size, and eight Nvidia L40S GPUs. The project address and promise to release code upon acceptance are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 40 reference entries are identical. The positioning relative to single-person generation, separate interaction modeling, InterGen, and RIG is unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 22 Nov 2024 to v3 dated 28 Feb 2025. This is a limited administrative text edit; the title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7, Tables 1–7, Algorithm 1, captions, and page layout are identical. Rendered pages match everywhere except the version/date characters in the first-page margin.

improvement.justification: The updated arXiv stamp does not change paper quality. Both PDFs provide identical scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation throughout the main text and appendices.
